what: the recurring line-forms by which THIS document marks its own divisions — speaker turns, chapter openings, section breaks — learned from the material's own regularities and held per-text; the division is received from the communicator, the typography that marks it is derived, and neither is assumed
notes: Recorded 2026-07-31, alongside its own counterexample. Seitsemän veljestä (pg11940) declares its cast 2321 times as a line-initial capital run followed by a period, and declares its chapters as LUKU headings; a reading that surveyed character n-grams instead consumed a surrogate for a book that had already named its speakers. But hardcoding that form is the opposite error and gets no tier at all: an assumed ^[A-Z]{2,}\. is a surface with no giver. The form must be learned from the material and then RECEIVED by the engine, which is why this sits in priors beside priors/coref/ rather than in the engine. Companion to document-who-for: the who-for is received, and so is the typography that carries it.
